body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the corrected handle \(\mathfrak I\) admits a measurable uniformly bounded right inverse on every observed-data DQM score: if \(s\in L^2_0(P)\) is the score of an observed path through \(P\), there are factorwise centered scores \(s_X,s_\pi,s_Y,s_A,s_Z\) such that
\[
s=E_P\{s_X(X)+s_\pi(J,X)+s_Y(Y,J,X)+s_A(A,J,X)+s_Z(Z,J,X)\mid O\},
\]
and the sum of their factor \(L^2\)-norms is at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\|s\|_{L^2(P)}\).  The recovery is measurable in \(X\), uses the augmented finite-feature inverse to fix the differentiated factorization, then uses the conditional \(G(X)^+\) solve for the measurement scores and the pointwise \(\{R^{\mathsf T}DR\}^{-1}\) solve for the remaining mixture and class-density scores.  Class-density scores are support preserving.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(s\in L^2_0(P)\) be the score of an observed-data DQM path.  Define
\[
 s_X(X)=E_P(s\mid X),\qquad s_c=s-s_X. \tag{79}
\]
Then \(E_P(s_c\mid X)=0\), and conditional Jensen gives
\(\|s_X\|_2\leq\|s\|_2\) and \(\|s_c\|_2\leq2\|s\|_2\).  For any bounded conditional moment \(H(O)\), DQM and Cauchy--Schwarz give its conditional derivative as \(E_P\{Hs_c\mid X\}\), with absolute value at most
\[
 \{E_P(H^2\mid X)\}^{1/2}\{E_P(s_c^2\mid X)\}^{1/2}. \tag{80}
\]
Apply Lemma 2A pointwise to the derivatives of the normalized finite moments.  Its uniform right-inverse bound and (80) yield measurable derivatives of \(\pi,M_A,M_Z,\Gamma_Y\) whose conditional Euclidean norm is at most
\[
 C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{E_P(s_c^2\mid X)\}^{1/2}. \tag{81}
\]
The modal permutation is locally constant by its positive gap, so it has no derivative.  Measurability follows because the recovered conditional moments have measurable versions on the standard Borel space \(\mathcal X\), and the finite inverse is Borel on the separated fixed-rank stratum.

To justify the cell-range relation used below without presupposing an \(L^2\) latent score, differentiate the identified density equation
\[
 p_A(y\mid x)=M_A(x)\Pi(x)f(y\mid x),
 \qquad \Pi=\operatorname{diag}(\pi), \tag{82}
\]
in conditional \(L^1(\nu)\).  Observed DQM implies this \(L^1\) derivative by Cauchy--Schwarz, and the uniformly bounded inverses in (82) give
\[
 \dot f=\Pi^{-1}M_A^{-1}
 \{\dot p_A-\dot M_A\Pi f-M_A\dot\Pi f\}. \tag{83}
\]
Its columns integrate to zero by normalization.  Common support permits the preliminary definition \(u_{Y,j}=\dot f_j/f_j\), \(f_jd\nu\)-almost everywhere.  Define \(u_{\pi,j}=\dot\pi_j/\pi_j\), and define each categorical factor score by derivative divided by a positive atom probability.  At a zero atom, a two-sided nonnegative probability path has derivative zero, and the score is set to zero.  Differentiating the product factorization now gives, almost everywhere,
\[
 s_c(y,a,z,x)=\sum_{j=1}^KR_{(a,z),j}(y,x)
 \{u_{\pi,j}(x)+u_{Y,j}(y,x)+u_{A,aj}(x)+u_{Z,zj}(x)\}. \tag{84}
\]
Equation (84) is used only to locate a finite-dimensional cell component; the following construction replaces these possibly ill-conditioned preliminary factor scores by a bounded-norm representation.

Let \(u\in\mathbb R^{2K^2}\) collect the measurement-score coordinates.  The terms in (84) depending only on \((Y,J,X)\) have cell vectors in \(\operatorname{range}(R)=\ker(N_B)\) by Lemma 3A, while the measurement contribution is \(c^{\mathsf T}u\).  Consequently,
\[
 N_Bs_c=h^{\mathsf T}u. \tag{85}
\]
Taking conditional inner products with \(h\) gives
\[
 b_s(X):=E_P(hN_Bs_c\mid X)=G(X)u. \tag{86}
\]
If \(v\in\ker G(X)\), then \(E_P\{(v^{\mathsf T}h)^2\mid X\}=0\), so \(v^{\mathsf T}h=0\) conditionally and \(v^{\mathsf T}b_s=0\).  Thus \(b_s\in\operatorname{range}(G)\).  Set \(u_0=G^+b_s\).  Since (86) has a solution, \(G(u_0-u)=0\), which implies \(h^{\mathsf T}(u_0-u)=0\), and hence
\[
 h^{\mathsf T}u_0=N_Bs_c. \tag{87}
\]
The projection-Gram gap and the least-squares projection identity give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|u_0(X)\|_2^2
 &=b_s^{\mathsf T}G^{+2}b_s
 \leq\varepsilon^{-1}b_s^{\mathsf T}G^+b_s\\
 &\leq\varepsilon^{-1}E_P\{(N_Bs_c)^2\mid X\}. \tag{88}
\end{aligned}
\]

For each latent-class block, subtract from the \(A\)-coordinates of \(u_0\) their \(M_A(\cdot\mid j,X)\)-mean, and do the analogous operation for \(Z\).  A blockwise constant has cell image proportional to \(R_{\cdot j}\), which \(N_B\) annihilates.  Thus recentering preserves (87).  Since the factors are probabilities and \(K\) is fixed, this operation multiplies the bound in (88) by at most a constant depending on \(K\).  Denote the centered coordinates by \((s_A,s_Z)\), and let \(c^{\mathsf T}u\) denote their observed cell contribution.

Set
\[
 s_0=s_c-c^{\mathsf T}u. \tag{89}
\]
Equation (87) implies \(N_Bs_0=0\).  Lemma 3A gives \(\ker(N_B)=\operatorname{range}(R)\), so pointwise
\[
 t(y,x)=\{R^{\mathsf T}DR\}^{-1}R^{\mathsf T}D
 s_0(y,\cdot,x),\qquad s_0=Rt. \tag{90}
\]
The inverse exists by the posterior-Gram gap.  Since
\(s_0^{\mathsf T}Ds_0=t^{\mathsf T}R^{\mathsf T}DRt\) and \(0\leq w_j\leq1\),
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^Kw_j(y,x)t_j(y,x)^2
 \leq\|t(y,x)\|_2^2
 \leq\varepsilon^{-1}s_0(y,\cdot,x)^{\mathsf T}D(y,x)s_0(y,\cdot,x). \tag{91}
\]
Define
\[
 s_{\pi,j}(x)=\int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid x)t_j(y,x)d\nu(y),
 \qquad
 s_{Y,j}(y,x)=t_j(y,x)-s_{\pi,j}(x). \tag{92}
\]
Then \(E_P(s_Y\mid J,X)=0\).  The recentered measurement contribution has conditional mean zero given \(X\), while \(E_P(s_c\mid X)=0\); integrating \(s_0=Rt\) and using \(g w_j=\pi_jf_j\) gives
\[
 0=E_P(s_0\mid X)=\sum_{j=1}^K\pi_j(X)s_{\pi,j}(X), \tag{93}
\]
the propensity-score centering condition.  Equations (89)--(93) give the exact conditional-expectation representation in the theorem.

Integrate (91) against \(g(y\mid x)d\nu(y)\).  Since \(gw_j=\pi_jf_j\), its left side is the conditional latent \(L^2\) norm of \(t\).  Jensen applied to (92) bounds the joint norms of \(s_\pi\) and \(s_Y\) by a constant times that norm.  The pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector is a contraction in \(D\)-norm, while \(d_{az}\geq\varepsilon\) converts this into a uniform Euclidean bound for \(N_B\).  Combining these facts with (88)--(91), the finite-dimensional bound on the centered measurement contribution, and (79), gives
\[
 \|s_X\|_2+\|s_\pi\|_2+\|s_Y\|_2+\|s_A\|_2+\|s_Z\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\|s\|_2. \tag{94}
\]
All conditional expectations admit measurable versions, and every finite inverse is Borel on the declared separated fixed-rank strata, so the construction is measurable in \(X\).  Finally, common support makes (92) an \(f_jd\nu\)-almost-everywhere density score on the original support; it assigns no mass outside that support.  Bounded truncation followed by \(f_j\)-recentering converges in the class-factor \(L^2\) norm and yields support-preserving two-sided exponential tilts wherever paths are required in the tangent closure.  This proves the asserted measurable uniformly bounded lift and support preservation.
